```{r setup}
# ============================================================
# Every number in this document is computed here or inline from
# saved aggregate results in the repository. Nothing is typed by
# hand except method constants. Missing files stop the render.
# Paths are relative to this file: the repository root is ../../..
# ============================================================
library(knitr)
ROOT <- normalizePath(file.path("..", "..", ".."))
OUT <- file.path(ROOT, "results", "benchmark_sim", "outputs")

#' Read a saved CSV under results/benchmark_sim/outputs, failing loudly.
#' @param ... path components below OUT
#' @return data.frame
rd <- function(...) {
  p <- file.path(OUT, ...)
  if (!file.exists(p)) stop("Missing saved evidence: ", p)
  read.csv(p, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

#' Read a CSV as it was saved at a given commit (registered results that
#' were later overwritten in place).
#' @param commit Git commit hash
#' @param path repository-relative path
#' @return data.frame
rd_git <- function(commit, path) {
  txt <- system2("git", c("-C", shQuote(ROOT), "show", paste0(commit, ":", path)),
                 stdout = TRUE, stderr = FALSE)
  if (!length(txt)) stop("Could not read ", path, " at ", commit)
  read.csv(text = paste(txt, collapse = "\n"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

# Number formatting: fixed decimals, a true minus sign, signed differences.
sci <- function(x) { e <- floor(log10(x)); paste0("$", formatC(x / 10^e, format = "f", digits = 0), " \\times 10^{", e, "}$") }
num <- function(x, d = 3) gsub("-", "−", formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d))
sgn <- function(x, d = 3) ifelse(x > 0, paste0("+", num(x, d)), num(x, d))
ci  <- function(lo, hi, d = 3) paste0(num(lo, d), " to ", num(hi, d))
pct <- function(x, d = 0) paste0(formatC(100 * x, format = "f", digits = d), "%")
big <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "d", big.mark = ",")

# Display names and platforms of the external series (design facts).
cohort_label <- c(Dijk = "Dijk", Moffitt_GEO_array = "Moffitt",
                  PACA_AU_array = "PACA-AU array", PACA_AU_seq = "PACA-AU RNA-seq",
                  Puleo_array = "Puleo")
cohort_platform <- c(Dijk = "RNA-seq", Moffitt_GEO_array = "Microarray",
                     PACA_AU_array = "Microarray", PACA_AU_seq = "RNA-seq",
                     Puleo_array = "Microarray")
```

# Summary {.unnumbered}

**Aim.** Bulk pancreatic tumors mix tumor, stromal and immune signals. We ask whether a Bayesian
matrix factorization that lets survival inform its molecular programs can find prognostic
programs that an unsupervised factorization misses, and whether its risk score transfers to new
cohorts.

**Method.** The model factorizes expression into patient activities and gene loadings and links
survival through a Cox model on the projection of each patient's expression onto the loadings.
A survival weight $w_S$ sets how much the Cox likelihood counts against the expression
likelihood. The comparator throughout is the same factorization at the same rank fitted without
survival, followed by a Cox model on its program scores.

**Results.** On `r train_n[["TCGA_PAAD"]] + train_n[["CPTAC"]]` training patients, five-fold
cross-validated concordance was `r num(cv_w1$mean_C)` for the supervised fit and
`r num(cv_ts$mean_C)` for the two-step fit. On five external series the mean concordance was
`r num(mean(e_w1$C))` against `r num(mean(e_ts$C))`, a pooled paired difference of
`r sgn(pool5$diff)` (95% interval `r ci(pool5$lo, pool5$hi)`). On these data survival supplies
at most `r sci(share_rng[2])` of the loading precision, so the supervised and unsupervised loadings are the
same and the small gain comes from estimating the coefficients jointly under a shrinkage prior. A
pre-registered October 15 check of an earlier supervised configuration gave a paired
difference of `r sgn(oct_reg_m$dC)` (95% interval `r ci(oct_reg_m$dC_lower, oct_reg_m$dC_upper)`).
Its lower limit fell below the non-inferiority margin. In simulation, supervision matches the two-step fit when a prognostic
program is easy to find and improves on it near the detection threshold.

# Methods {#sec-methods}

## Notation {#sec-notation}

Patients are indexed by $i = 1, \dots, n$, genes by $j = 1, \dots, p$ and programs (factors) by
$k = 1, \dots, K$. Patient $i$ has observed time $t_i$ and event indicator $\delta_i$ (1 for
death, 0 for censoring). The training data are an $n \times p$ expression matrix $Y$. For a
random quantity $\theta$ under the variational posterior $q$, $\bar\theta = E_q\theta$.

Two patient-level quantities are kept apart. The **activities** $L \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times K}$
are posterior scores in the reconstruction $Y \approx LF^\top$ and exist only for training
patients. The **program scores** $Z = Y\bar F$ are the product of a patient's expression with
the posterior-mean loadings. They enter the Cox predictor and can be computed for any new
patient whose expression is measured on the same genes.

## Model {#sec-model}

The expression matrix is modeled as
$$
y_{ij} = \sum_{k=1}^K L_{ik} F_{jk} + e_{ij}, \qquad e_{ij} \sim N(0, \tau_j^{-1}),
$$ {#eq-recon}
with independent point-Laplace priors on the entries of each column of $L$ and $F$, a point mass
at zero mixed with a Laplace distribution, whose parameters are estimated by empirical Bayes
within each program with the R package ebnm [@Willwerscheid2025]. Each gene has its own residual
precision $\tau_j$. Survival follows a Cox model [@Cox1972] whose linear predictor is the
program-score projection,
$$
\eta_i = \sum_{k=1}^K Z_{ik}\beta_k, \qquad Z = Y\bar F, \qquad \beta_k \sim N(0, \sigma_k^2),
$$ {#eq-eta}
with the prior variance $\sigma_k^2$ estimated per program. This is the YFB model, named for its
predictor $\eta = (YF)\beta$. Because new patients are scored by the same projection, prediction
needs no refitting.

The variational objective is
$$
E_q \log p(Y \mid L, F, \tau) \;+\; w_S\, E_q \log \mathrm{PL}(\beta, F) \;-\; \mathrm{KL}(q \,\|\, \text{prior}),
$$ {#eq-objective}
where $\mathrm{PL}$ is the Cox partial likelihood. The survival weight $w_S$ multiplies the Cox
term wherever it appears: in the loading update, in the coefficient update and in the objective.
At $w_S = 1$ the objective is the evidence lower bound of the joint model. Larger values of $w_S$
give survival more influence on the loadings. The full derivation, with every update checked
term by term against the code, is in
`derivations/SSBMF-YFB-model-derivations/SSBMF-YFB-model-derivation-full.pdf` (Appendix A).

**Scale.** The reconstruction does not fix the scale of a program: multiplying $L_{\cdot k}$ by
$c$ and dividing $F_{\cdot k}$ by $c$ leaves $LF^\top$ unchanged. The fit therefore rescales
each program after its update so that its training program score has standard deviation 1. Each
$\beta_k$ is then a log hazard ratio per standard deviation of the program score, and a single
$w_S$ means the same thing for every program.

## Fitting and prediction {#sec-fitting}

Each sweep re-expands the Cox partial likelihood to second order around the current
$\bar\eta$, with the predictor's variance taken from $q(\beta)$ and $q(F)$. It then updates, one
program at a time, the activities, the loadings (from the reconstruction residual and the
weighted Cox term) and the coefficient, and finally the precisions. The fit starts from the
singular value decomposition of $Y$ and stops when the relative change in the objective falls
below $10^{-5}$ or after 300 sweeps. The rank is fixed at $K = 7$ and no program is removed.

New cohorts are standardized gene by gene within cohort and scored on the training genes they
measure. The direction of the risk score is the one the fit learns from training survival. There
is no post-fit sign correction: a fit oriented the wrong way would have training concordance
below 0.5 and is reported as fitted.

## The two-step comparator {#sec-two-step}

The comparison that isolates the effect of supervision uses the same fitter at $w_S = 0$, which
removes survival from the loading update and gives the unsupervised empirical-Bayes
factorization at the same rank, on the same genes and patients. Because $w_S$ also multiplies the
Cox term in the coefficient update, $w_S = 0$ gives $\beta = 0$. The two-step comparator
therefore takes the $w_S = 0$ loadings and fits an unpenalized Cox model on the training program
scores. It differs from the supervised fit only in whether survival entered the loadings and in
how $\beta$ was estimated.

## Choosing the survival weight {#sec-weight}

The current real-data configuration uses $w_S = 1$, fixed by five-fold training cross-validation
(@sec-results-fair). Two refinements were then tested in simulation. In the survival-block form,
$w_S$ multiplies the Cox term and the Kullback–Leibler term of $\beta$ together, so $\beta$ gets
an ordinary Bayesian Cox fit while the loadings see survival at weight $w_S$. The weight is
chosen for each dataset from $\{1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50\}$ by five-fold cross-validated partial
log-likelihood, with ties going to the smaller weight. Applying this rule to the real training
data (study S-15) is complete (@sec-results-s15).

## Earlier configuration {#sec-earlier}

The October 16 version of this writeup evaluated a different fitter configuration, in which the
loading weight $\alpha_F$ was 0 and survival never entered the loading update. That model is an
unsupervised factorization followed by a Cox fit with a shrinkage prior. It cannot find a
prognostic program that explains little expression variance, which is the reason for the
supervised method, so it is no longer the proposed model. Its external results are kept as a
historical reference and are reported here under the corrected preprocessing (@sec-results-alpha0).

# Evaluation {#sec-evaluation}

## Data {#sec-data}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-cohorts
#| tbl-cap: "Training and validation cohorts. Patient and death counts are read from the saved fold table and external scoring results. Missing genes are training genes not measured in the external series; those genes do not enter its score. PACA-AU is the Australian pancreatic cancer project of the International Cancer Genome Consortium (ICGC). Its array and RNA-seq series share donors (@sec-data). TCGA-PAAD, The Cancer Genome Atlas pancreatic adenocarcinoma cohort; CPTAC, Clinical Proteomic Tumor Analysis Consortium; RNA-seq, RNA sequencing."
tab <- rbind(
  data.frame(Cohort = c("TCGA-PAAD", "CPTAC"), Platform = "RNA-seq",
             Patients = as.integer(train_n[c("TCGA_PAAD", "CPTAC")]),
             Deaths = as.integer(train_d[c("TCGA_PAAD", "CPTAC")]),
             `Missing genes` = 0L, Role = "Training", check.names = FALSE),
  data.frame(Cohort = cohort_label[e_w1$cohort], Platform = cohort_platform[e_w1$cohort],
             Patients = e_w1$n, Deaths = e_w1$events, `Missing genes` = e_w1$missing_genes,
             Role = "External validation", check.names = FALSE))
kable(tab, row.names = FALSE, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

The model is trained on `r train_n[["TCGA_PAAD"]] + train_n[["CPTAC"]]` patients
(`r train_d[["TCGA_PAAD"]] + train_d[["CPTAC"]]` deaths) from two RNA-seq cohorts, TCGA-PAAD and
CPTAC (@tbl-cohorts). Every RNA-seq cohort is transformed once by $\log_2(x+1)$. Earlier
benchmarks applied this transform twice to three RNA-seq cohorts, an error found in review and
corrected on October 30. Genes are screened separately in each training cohort by the combined
mean and variance rank of DeSurv [@Young2026], keeping the top 3,000 per cohort. The
intersection, called the D4 gene set, has `r big(genes$n_genes[genes$arm == "single"])` genes
under the single log. Each cohort is then standardized gene by gene to mean 0 and standard
deviation 1.

The five external series supply `r big(ext_records)` records and `r big(ext_deaths)` deaths.
These are not counts of distinct people. The PACA-AU array and RNA-seq series share `r donors$shared_donors` donors,
and the RNA-seq series has `r donors$seq_records` records from `r donors$seq_donors` donors,
so the external collection represents `r ext_people`
people if the other cohorts are distinct (counts from the October 16 accuracy review,
`paper/writeup/2026-10-16-writeup/_process/Accuracy_Review_Dispositions_10_16_26.md`).

## Uses of the external cohorts {#sec-external-uses}

The five external series have been scored in every benchmark since May 2026, and several of
those scorings chose or informed a setting that the current model still uses. @tbl-external-uses
lists every such use found in the decision log. The column "In the current model" says whether
the setting survives in the supervised fit of @sec-model.

| Choice | Date | How the external series entered | In the current model | Record |
|----------------|------|----------------------------|----------|------------|
| Within-cohort standardization, no rank transform (one of 18 preprocessing configurations) | May 25 | Chosen outright: highest mean external C | Yes | DECISIONS.md, 2026-05-25 |
| D4 gene screen (per-cohort combined mean and variance rank) | May 27 | Chosen outright: adopted because external C rose by more than a set threshold | Yes | DECISIONS.md, 2026-05-27 |
| Pooled fit without cohort indicators | May 22–27 | Informed: external C compared alongside a training diagnosis | Yes | DECISIONS.md, 2026-05-22 to 2026-05-27 |
| Rank $K = 7$ | May to August | First set by training cross-validation; later kept after external comparisons (ranks 5 and 6 excluded on external C on August 19, external plateau from rank 7 in the August 27 sweep) | Yes | DECISIONS.md, 2026-08-19 and 2026-08-27 |
| Loading weight $\alpha_F = 0$ and frozen-loading start $N_{\mathrm{frozen}}$ | August 20 | The defaults predate external use. A 16-cell grid scored externally kept both, since no setting won clearly | No: the current fitter uses $w_S$ | DECISIONS.md, 2026-08-20 |
| Two-step comparator configuration (rank 7, 20 or 40, with or without LASSO) | July 16 to August 20 | Arms compared and chosen on external C | No: replaced by the $w_S = 0$ two-step fit | DECISIONS.md, 2026-08-20 |
| October 15 supervised configuration | October 15 | Chosen in simulation, then scored once against a registered criterion (@sec-results-oct15) | Superseded | DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-15 |
| Single-log correction | October 26 | Scored once to measure the effect. Nothing chosen | Yes (single log) | `docs/findings/2026-10-26-single-log-check.md` |
| Current supervised fit ($w_S = 1$, D4, no screen) | November 5 | Fixed by training cross-validation, then scored once (@sec-results-fair) | Yes | `docs/findings/2026-11-05-supervised-external-scoring-findings.md` |

: Every use of the five external series in a model-development choice, from the project decision log. "Chosen outright" means external concordance was the deciding criterion. "Informed" means it was one of several pieces of evidence. C, Harrell's concordance index; LASSO, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator. {#tbl-external-uses}

The gene screen, the standardization and the rank of the current model therefore all descend
from choices made with external concordance. No external series is untouched by every choice,
and the external results in this writeup are development-informed, not independent validation.
The training cross-validation of @sec-results-fair fixed only the survival weight, the gene-set
size and the screening arm, within this inherited setup. Holding back one cohort from every
remaining choice is listed under continuing work.

## Simulation designs {#sec-sim-designs}

All three simulation studies plant a single prognostic program among unsupervised structure and
ask whether the fit recovers it. A program counts as recovered when the absolute correlation
between its estimated and planted loadings is at least 0.7. A **false-active** program is one
whose coefficient lies more than 1.96 posterior standard deviations from zero but which does not
match the planted program.

- **Survival weight at 2,000 genes (S-9).** Data with $p = 50$ or $2{,}000$ genes and a planted
  program carrying 0.25%, 1% or 5% of the expression variance, ten datasets per cell, fitted at
  $w_S \in \{0, 1, 10, 100, 1{,}000, 10{,}000\}$, at $w_S = p/50$ and at a weight calibrated to give
  survival 20% of the loading precision. The planted survival
  effect is strong: validation concordance of the true predictor is about 0.94 to 0.99.
- **Weight chosen by cross-validation (S-13).** The $p = 2{,}000$ cells of S-9 plus a cell with
  weaker survival, ten datasets each, with the weight chosen per dataset by the rule of
  @sec-weight. Two arms differ in the coefficient posterior: mean-field (A1) or a joint Gaussian
  posterior for $\beta$ (A2).
- **Programs near the detection threshold (S-14).** Planted programs carrying 0.05%, 0.1% or 0.2%
  of the expression variance, with strong survival (oracle concordance about 0.94) or realistic
  survival (oracle concordance about 0.74), ten datasets per cell.

Each study compares the supervised fit with the two-step comparator of @sec-two-step fitted to
the same data.

## Performance metrics and uncertainty {#sec-metrics}

Discrimination is Harrell's concordance index C [@Harrell1982], with the risk direction fixed
from training. Paired differences between two models use percentile bootstrap intervals
[@EfronTibshirani1993] from resampling patients within each cohort, with both models scored on
the same resamples. The pooled difference across cohorts is stratified by cohort. Calibration is
the slope of a Cox regression of held-out survival on the fitted risk score: a slope of 1 means
the fitted risk differences have the right size, a slope above 1 means they are too small and a
slope below 1 means they are too large. In simulation the slopes use exact event times, because
the default tie handling of `survival::coxph()` merges the extreme simulated times and flattens
every slope.

The external bootstrap resamples records, not donors. The `r donors$shared_donors` donors shared by the two PACA-AU
series are counted twice in a pooled estimate, so each pooled difference is also reported without
the PACA-AU RNA-seq series. Intervals hold the fitted models fixed and do not include training
uncertainty.

# Results {#sec-results}

## Supervised fit against the rank-7 two-step fit {#sec-results-fair}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-cv
#| tbl-cap: "Five-fold training cross-validation on the 2,218 D4 genes (single log). Both fits have rank 7 and use the same folds. The two-step fit takes the loadings of the w_S = 0 fit and fits a Cox model on the training program scores. Survival-active: coefficient at least 1.96 posterior standard deviations from zero in the fit to all training patients (Wald test for the two-step fit). C, Harrell's concordance index; SE, standard error across folds; PL, partial log-likelihood."
cvt <- data.frame(
  Fit = c("Supervised, w_S = 1", "Two-step (w_S = 0 loadings, then Cox)"),
  `Mean fold C (SE)` = c(paste0(num(cv_w1$mean_C), " (", num(cv_w1$se_C), ")"),
                         paste0(num(cv_ts$mean_C), " (", num(cv_ts$se_C), ")")),
  `Pooled out-of-fold C` = num(c(cv_w1$pooled_oof_C, cv_ts$pooled_oof_C)),
  `CV partial log-likelihood` = num(c(cv_w1$cv_partial_loglik, cv_ts$cv_partial_loglik), 1),
  `Folds converged` = paste0(c(cv_w1$folds_converged, cv_ts$folds_converged), " of 5"),
  `Survival-active` = c(cv_w1$full_active, cv_ts$full_active), check.names = FALSE)
kable(cvt, row.names = FALSE)
```

On the training patients, the supervised fit had mean fold concordance `r num(cv_w1$mean_C)`
against `r num(cv_ts$mean_C)` for the two-step fit (@tbl-cv). The paired fold difference was
`r sgn(cv_diff)` (SE `r num(cv_diff_se)`). In `r 5 - cv_conv` of the five folds both fits reached
the 300-sweep cap with the objective still changing slowly. Their coefficients were small, and no
coefficient or noise precision was growing, so these folds were moving slowly near their optimum
rather than diverging.

This configuration ($w_S = 1$, the D4 genes, no survival screen) was fixed from these training
results before any external cohort was scored. It was then scored once on the five external
series (@tbl-external).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-external
#| tbl-cap: "External concordance of the fixed supervised fit and the two-step fit. Each series was scored once, after the configuration was fixed by training cross-validation. C intervals are 95% percentile bootstrap intervals over patients. The difference is supervised minus two-step on the same resamples. Pooled rows stratify by cohort. Because the PACA-AU series share donors, the pooled difference is also given without the RNA-seq series. The calibration slope is the coefficient of held-out survival on the fitted risk score; 1 is calibrated."
ord <- match(e_w1$cohort, e_ts$cohort)
xt <- data.frame(
  Series = cohort_label[e_w1$cohort],
  `C, supervised (95% CI)` = paste0(num(e_w1$C), " (", ci(e_w1$lo, e_w1$hi), ")"),
  `C, two-step` = num(e_ts$C[ord]),
  `Difference (95% CI)` = paste0(sgn(extd$diff[match(e_w1$cohort, extd$cohort)]), " (",
    ci(extd$lo[match(e_w1$cohort, extd$cohort)], extd$hi[match(e_w1$cohort, extd$cohort)]), ")"),
  `Slope, supervised` = num(e_w1$cal_slope, 2),
  `Slope, two-step` = num(e_ts$cal_slope[ord], 2), check.names = FALSE)
xt <- rbind(xt,
  data.frame(Series = "Mean of five series", `C, supervised (95% CI)` = num(mean(e_w1$C)),
             `C, two-step` = num(mean(e_ts$C)), `Difference (95% CI)` = "",
             `Slope, supervised` = "", `Slope, two-step` = "", check.names = FALSE),
  data.frame(Series = "Pooled, stratified", `C, supervised (95% CI)` = "", `C, two-step` = "",
             `Difference (95% CI)` = paste0(sgn(pool5$diff), " (", ci(pool5$lo, pool5$hi), ")"),
             `Slope, supervised` = "", `Slope, two-step` = "", check.names = FALSE),
  data.frame(Series = "Pooled, without PACA-AU RNA-seq", `C, supervised (95% CI)` = "",
             `C, two-step` = "",
             `Difference (95% CI)` = paste0(sgn(poolns$diff), " (", ci(poolns$lo, poolns$hi), ")"),
             `Slope, supervised` = "", `Slope, two-step` = "", check.names = FALSE))
kable(xt, row.names = FALSE)
```

The supervised fit scored equal to or higher than the two-step fit in every series. Its mean
external concordance was `r num(mean(e_w1$C))` and the two-step fit's `r num(mean(e_ts$C))`. The
pooled paired difference was `r sgn(pool5$diff)` (95% interval `r ci(pool5$lo, pool5$hi)`), and
`r sgn(poolns$diff)` (`r ci(poolns$lo, poolns$hi)`) without the PACA-AU RNA-seq series. Both
intervals include zero. The difference is about the size of the training cross-validation
difference. Dijk and Moffitt were the weakest series for both fits, as they were for every
earlier model.

The supervised fit's calibration slopes were closer to 1 than the two-step fit's in
`r sum(abs(log(e_w1$cal_slope)) < abs(log(e_ts$cal_slope[ord])))` of five series, ranging from `r num(min(e_w1$cal_slope), 2)` to `r num(max(e_w1$cal_slope), 2)`, with
`r num(e_w1$cal_slope[e_w1$cohort == "Puleo_array"], 2)` in Puleo, the largest series. The
two-step slopes were below 1 in `r sum(e_ts$cal_slope < 1)` of five series, which is what an unpenalized Cox fit on
seven correlated scores tends to give: risk differences that are too large out of sample. As a
summary on the scale DeSurv reports [@Young2026], the hazard ratio per standard deviation of the
risk score, from a Cox model stratified by series over all `r big(exth$n[1])` records, was
`r num(exth$hr_per_sd[exth$model == "w1"], 2)` (95% CI
`r ci(exth$lo[exth$model == "w1"], exth$hi[exth$model == "w1"], 2)`) for the supervised fit and
`r num(exth$hr_per_sd[exth$model == "twostep"], 2)`
(`r ci(exth$lo[exth$model == "twostep"], exth$hi[exth$model == "twostep"], 2)`) for the two-step
fit.

## The pre-registered October 15 supervision check {#sec-results-oct15}

On October 15 an earlier supervised configuration was evaluated against a criterion fixed before
it ran. That configuration used the same predictor with $w_S = 1$, a supervised start and a
shared point-Laplace prior on $\beta$, on the 2,064 genes of the historical preprocessing. In
simulation it recovered a planted low-variance prognostic program in `r oct_sim$recovered[oct_sim$noise == 0.25]` of `r oct_n[["0.25"]]` datasets at the
lower noise level and `r oct_sim$recovered[oct_sim$noise == 1]` of `r oct_n[["1"]]` at the higher one. The registered real-data estimand was the mean
over the five external series of the per-series difference in C from the frozen $\alpha_F = 0$
benchmark, with a cohort-stratified paired bootstrap. The criterion was a lower 95% limit above
`r num(oct_margin, 2)`.

The estimate was `r sgn(oct_reg_m$dC)` (95% interval
`r ci(oct_reg_m$dC_lower, oct_reg_m$dC_upper)`). The lower limit missed the margin, so **the
criterion was not met**. External concordance was unchanged within the precision that five
cohorts allow, which is not the same as showing no loss. Mean external C was
`r num(oct_reg_m$C_arm)` for the supervised fit and `r num(oct_reg_m$C_D4)` for the benchmark.
After the KL normalizer was corrected later the same day, the refit gave
`r sgn(oct_now_m$dC)` (`r ci(oct_now_m$dC_lower, oct_now_m$dC_upper)`), which also misses the
margin. The registered values are read from the result file as committed at the time (commit
`65cf90a`), and the rerun values from the current file. Work continued with the configuration
recorded as not meeting the criterion (DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-15).

## What survival does to the real-data loadings {#sec-results-loadings}

On the training data at $w_S = 1$, survival supplies between
`r sci(share_rng[1])` and `r sci(share_rng[2])` of the loading precision (median over
programs, across the gene-set sizes below). In simulation the corresponding share was 0.01 to 0.2
at 2,000 genes. Two things keep it small on real data. The fitted coefficients are small
(largest $|\bar\beta_k|$ `r num(full_w1$max_abs_beta, 2)` per standard deviation of the program
score), and the share scales with $E[\beta_k^2]$. The real programs also explain much more
expression variance than the planted programs in simulation, so their expression precision is
large. As a result the supervised and unsupervised loadings agree to $|r| = 1.000$ for every
program, and the two fits have the same top genes. The concordance gain of
@sec-results-fair comes from estimating $\beta$ jointly with a shrinkage prior, not from survival
moving the loadings.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-size
#| tbl-cap: "Training cross-validation by input gene-set size. Sets are nested and outcome-free, ranked by the per-cohort mean and variance rank; D4 is the 2,218-gene default. Match: absolute loading correlations of the two survival-active programs of the all-genes supervised fit with their best matches at each size."
w <- sizes[sizes$arm == "w1", ]; t2 <- sizes[sizes$arm == "w0cox", ]
ag <- s11_agree[s11_agree$arm == "w1", ]
st <- data.frame(Genes = big(w$n_genes),
  `Supervised C (SE)` = paste0(num(w$mean_C), " (", num(w$se_C), ")"),
  `Two-step C (SE)` = paste0(num(t2$mean_C[match(w$set, t2$set)]), " (", num(t2$se_C[match(w$set, t2$set)]), ")"),
  `Folds converged, supervised` = w$folds_converged,
  Match = ag$matches[match(w$set, ag$set)], check.names = FALSE)
kable(st, row.names = FALSE)
```

Adding genes beyond the D4 set did not help (@tbl-size). Supervised concordance ranged from
`r num(min(w$mean_C))` to `r num(max(w$mean_C))` across sizes, and every size was within one
standard error of the others. The registered rule, which picks the smallest set within one
standard error of the all-genes concordance whose survival-active programs match the all-genes
fit at $|r| \ge 0.7$, chose D4 for both fits. The supervised advantage over the two-step fit
shrank as genes were added and reversed above 5,000 genes.

Screening genes on survival inside each training fold, by a cohort-stratified univariable Cox
test, gave no consistent gain over an outcome-free screen of the same size: the paired
differences were `r ci(min(s11_scr$diff_S_minus_U), max(s11_scr$diff_S_minus_U))` across sizes
and fits, each within about one paired standard error, and no screened set beat the supervised
fit on all D4 genes. With survival permuted in simulated data, the $w_S = 1$ fit had
`r num(min(s11_null$n_active), 1)` to `r num(max(s11_null$n_active), 1)` false-active programs per
dataset on average, below the registered limit of one.

## Simulation: supervision strength and the weight choice {#sec-results-weight}

At $w_S = 1$ and 2,000 genes the fit recovered the planted program in
`r paste(s9_w1_2k$recovered, collapse = ", ")` of 10 datasets in the three variance cells, with
mean false-active counts `r paste(num(s9_w1_2k$mean_false_active, 1), collapse = ", ")`, and every
fit converged. No fit at $w_S = 40$ or more converged within 300 sweeps at 2,000 genes, and recovery fell in most of those cells. The
coefficients at $w_S = 1$ were attenuated: median validation calibration slopes were
`r paste(num(s9_w1_2k$cal_slope_median, 2), collapse = ", ")` across the three cells, where the
true predictor gives about 1. Ranking was good (mean validation C
`r ci(min(s9_w1_2k$c_validation_mean), max(s9_w1_2k$c_validation_mean))`), so the attenuation
affects the size of predicted risk differences, not their order.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-s13
#| tbl-cap: "Weight chosen by five-fold cross-validated partial log-likelihood (S-13), against the two-step fit on the same datasets. Cells v0.0025, v0.01 and v0.05 are the 2,000-gene S-9 cells by planted variance share; weak is a cell with weaker survival. Ten datasets per cell. Recovered counts are out of 10. FA, mean number of false-active programs; C, mean validation concordance; slope, median calibration slope with exact event times."
x <- s13
kable(data.frame(Arm = x$arm, Cell = x$cell, `Chosen weights (count)` = x$weights,
  Recovered = x$recovered, `Two-step recovered` = x$twostep_recovered,
  FA = num(x$mean_false_active, 1), `Two-step FA` = num(x$twostep_false_active, 1),
  C = num(x$c_validation), `Two-step C` = num(x$twostep_c),
  Slope = num(x$slope_median, 2), `Two-step slope` = num(x$twostep_slope, 2),
  check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE)
```

Choosing the weight by cross-validation worked as a rule (@tbl-s13). The chosen weight rose with
the strength of the planted program, from 1 or 2 in the weak and 0.25% cells to 10 in the 5%
cell, and the rule never chose 20 or 50, at which full fits stopped converging. At the chosen
weight the supervised fit and the two-step fit recovered the program in every dataset, and
validation concordance differed by at most
`r num(max(abs(s13$c_validation - s13$twostep_c)))`. In these cells, then, supervision matches
the two-step fit rather than improving on it. Neither arm met every registered criterion: the
median calibration slope fell inside the registered band of 0.8 to 1.25 in
`r s13v$slope_cells[1]` of 3 cells for each arm, and the mean-field arm's null false-active count
was `r num(s13v$null_max_false_active[s13v$arm == "A1"], 1)` against a limit of 1. Nothing from
S-13 was adopted. The joint coefficient posterior changed validation concordance by at most a few
thousandths, so it stays optional.

Phase 2: add the Chapter 4 weight-curve figure (its F1) with its caption.

## Simulation: programs near the detection threshold {#sec-results-threshold}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-s14
#| tbl-cap: "Programs near the detection threshold (S-14). Ten datasets per cell; all fits converged. Planted share is the planted program's share of expression variance. Recovered counts are out of 10. Difference is the mean paired validation C of the supervised fit at w_S = 1 minus the two-step fit, with the number of datasets in which the supervised fit was higher. Oracle C is the validation concordance of the true predictor."
a <- s14a[s14a$arm %in% c("twostep", "A1_w1"), ]
w1 <- a[a$arm == "A1_w1", ]; ts <- a[a$arm == "twostep", ]
k <- match(paste(w1$strength, w1$share), paste(ts$strength, ts$share))
dd <- s14d[match(paste(w1$strength, w1$share), paste(s14d$strength, s14d$share)), ]
tt <- data.frame(Survival = w1$strength, `Planted share` = pct(w1$share, 2),
  `Recovered, supervised` = round(10 * w1$recovered), `Recovered, two-step` = round(10 * ts$recovered[k]),
  `FA, supervised` = num(w1$false_active, 1), `FA, two-step` = num(ts$false_active[k], 1),
  `C, supervised` = num(w1$c_validation), `C, two-step` = num(ts$c_validation[k]),
  `Difference (higher of 10)` = paste0(sgn(dd$d.mean), " (", dd$d.wins, ")"),
  `Oracle C` = num(w1$oracle_c), check.names = FALSE)
tt <- tt[order(tt$Survival, w1$share), ]
kable(tt, row.names = FALSE)
```

In the S-9 and S-13 cells the two-step fit already finds the planted program, so those studies
cannot show what supervision adds. S-14 planted weaker programs (@tbl-s14). With strong survival
the supervised fit had the higher validation concordance in
`r sum(s14p$d[s14p$strength == "strong"] > 0)` of `r sum(s14p$strength == "strong")` datasets,
and the gain grew as the program weakened. At a planted share of 0.05% the supervised fit
recovered the program in `r round(10 * w1$recovered[w1$strength == "strong" & w1$share == 5e-4])`
of 10 datasets, where the two-step fit recovered none, and validation concordance rose by
`r sgn(s14d$d.mean[s14d$strength == "strong" & s14d$share == 5e-4])`. With realistic survival the
two fits were close at 0.1% and 0.2%, and neither recovered the 0.05% program. The registered
recovery criterion still failed in every strong cell, because it also limited the mean
false-active count to 1. The two-step fit had as many or more false-active programs in the same
cells.

The false-active programs matter little for prediction. Where the planted program was recovered,
the other active programs carried at most a few percent of the risk-score variance, and removing
them changed validation concordance by at most
`r num(max(abs(fa13$delta_c), na.rm = TRUE))` in S-13. Where the program was only partly found,
at a share of 0.05%, the other programs carried part of the planted direction and added to
concordance. That split was much larger for the two-step fit than for the supervised fit
(`docs/findings/2026-11-05-near-threshold-findings.md`).

::: {.draft-note}
Phase 2: add the Chapter 4 paired-concordance figure for S-14 with its caption.
:::

## Real-data refit at the cross-validated weight {#sec-results-s15}

On the training folds, the largest cross-validated partial log-likelihood occurred at
$w_S = `r s15$w_star`$. Across the grid from `r min(s15_curve$w)` to `r max(s15_curve$w)`,
the partial log-likelihood varied by `r num(diff(range(s15_curve$cvpl)), 2)`. Nested
cross-validation gave mean C of `r num(s15$nested_mean_C)` (SE `r num(s15$nested_se_C)`).
The registered rule retained the existing fit because the selected weight matched it.
External scoring was limited to the previously fixed comparison in @sec-results-fair.

## The α~F~ = 0 benchmark under the single log {#sec-results-alpha0}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-alpha0
#| tbl-cap: "External concordance of the earlier alpha_F = 0 benchmark (rank 7, survival absent from the loading update), as frozen under the double log and refitted with every cohort logged once. The difference interval is a 95% percentile bootstrap over patients within each series. Risk-score correlation compares the two fits' external scores."
kable(data.frame(Series = cohort_label[slog_c$cohort], n = slog_c$n,
  `Frozen (double log)` = num(slog_c$C_frozen), `Single log` = num(slog_c$C_single),
  `Difference (95% CI)` = paste0(sgn(slog_c$diff_single_minus_frozen), " (",
    ci(slog_c$diff_ci_lo, slog_c$diff_ci_hi), ")"),
  `Risk-score correlation` = num(slog_c$risk_cor_single_frozen), check.names = FALSE),
  row.names = FALSE)
```

The earlier benchmark's external numbers were computed under the double log. Refitted with every
cohort logged once and nothing else changed, its mean external concordance was
`r num(slog_m$C_single)` against `r num(slog_m$C_frozen)` frozen, every per-series interval
included zero, and the risk scores correlated at
`r num(min(slog_c$risk_cor_single_frozen), 2)` or more (@tbl-alpha0). The single-log number is
the one to compare with. It is not a paired comparison with the supervised fit of
@sec-results-fair, which uses a different fitter, input scaling and gene set. After the KL fix, all
`r slog_cv$n_converged[slog_cv$arm == "single"]` single-log folds converged. Training
cross-validated C was `r num(slog_cv$mean_C[slog_cv$arm == "single"])` with the single log and
`r num(slog_cv$mean_C[slog_cv$arm == "double"])` with the double log.

The October 16 writeup led with a comparison against a 40-factor unsupervised factorization
followed by LASSO Cox (`r num(slog_m$C_frozen)` against `r num(k40_mean)`). That comparator was run only under the double log,
and its factor cap was not matched to the model, so it is not used here. Against the
rank-matched two-step model the earlier benchmark's advantage was `r num(k7$diff_estimate)` (95% interval
`r ci(k7$diff_lower, k7$diff_upper)`), the same small size as the supervised fit's advantage in @sec-results-fair.

# Programs of the supervised fit {#sec-biology}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-programs
#| tbl-cap: "Programs of the supervised fit on all training patients (w_S = 1, D4 genes). The coefficient is the log hazard ratio per standard deviation of the program score; positive means a higher score raises the hazard. Active: coefficient at least 1.96 posterior SD from zero. Five genes with the largest positive and negative loadings are listed."
p <- s11_prog[s11_prog$arm == "w1", ]
top5 <- function(s) paste(head(strsplit(s, " ")[[1]], 5), collapse = ", ")
p <- p[order(-abs(p$z)), ]
kable(data.frame(Program = p$program, `β (SD)` = paste0(num(p$beta, 2), " (", num(p$beta_sd, 2), ")"),
  Active = ifelse(p$survival_active, "yes", "no"),
  `Positive pole` = vapply(p$top_positive, top5, ""), `Negative pole` = vapply(p$top_negative, top5, ""),
  check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE)
```

The fit to all training patients keeps all seven programs, and `r sum(p$survival_active)` are
survival-active (@tbl-programs). From their top genes they are a hypoxia and glycolysis versus
normal-pancreas axis, protective at its normal pole, a ribosomal and proliferation versus
classical-epithelial axis, adverse at its proliferative pole, and a third adverse program. The
two-step fit has the same programs and top genes, as @sec-results-loadings implies. The prior on
$\beta$ shrinks two programs to essentially zero, where the unpenalized Cox fit gives them small
nonzero coefficients.

# Discussion {#sec-discussion}

## Interpretation {#sec-interpretation}

On the real data the supervised fit predicts about as well as the same factorization followed by
Cox, with a small gain in concordance whose interval includes zero and with better calibrated
risk differences. Survival does not change its loadings at the current weight, so this is not
yet evidence of survival-guided discovery. The gain comes from the coefficient update and its
shrinkage prior. The simulation studies show where supervision should help. When a prognostic
program explains enough expression variance, the unsupervised factorization already finds it, and
supervision changes nothing. When the program sits near the detection threshold and survival
carries strong information, supervision finds programs the two-step fit misses and predicts
better. Real PDAC survival is closer to the realistic setting of S-14, where the gain was small.

## Limitations {#sec-limitations}

The external series are not independent of every model choice (@sec-external-uses). In
particular the rank $K = 7$ was carried over from earlier work in which external concordance
informed it, so no series is untouched. The bootstrap resamples records, and the `r donors$shared_donors` donors shared
by the PACA-AU series enter the pooled estimates twice. Dropping the smaller series barely moves
the pooled difference, but donor-level resampling has not been run. Two of the five supervised
training folds stopped at the sweep cap. In simulation the coefficients at $w_S = 1$ are
attenuated at 2,000 genes, and every simulation uses one generator with ten datasets per cell.

## Continuing work {#sec-continuing}

- **Supervision strength set from the data.** At $w_S = 1$ survival does not move the real
  loadings, and fixed weights of 40 or more broke convergence in simulation. Candidates are the
  a calibrated power on the Cox likelihood, a downweighted
  expression term and normalized loss terms as in DeSurv.
- **Multiple modalities.** A model with shared activities and modality-specific loadings and
  loading priors, of which the present model is the case $M = 1$. It is derived but deferred
  until single-modality supervision meets its acceptance criteria. The October multimodal results
  are in the October 16 version.
- **Rank selection.** $K$ is fixed at 7. A rule that does not use validation outcomes is needed.
- **Comparators.** PurIST as a prognostic comparator [@Rashid2020], DeSurv head to head, an
  elastic-net Cox model on genes, and a model with clinical covariates.
- **Inference.** Donor-level resampling for the PACA-AU series, and one external cohort held back
  from every remaining choice.

# Appendix A. Model derivation {#sec-appendix-a .unnumbered}

::: {.draft-note}
Phase 2: a one-page algorithm summary from the full derivation.
:::

The complete derivation of the current fit, from the joint model to the algorithm, with the
balance of expression and survival information in the loading update and an errata table for the
earlier pieces, is
`derivations/SSBMF-YFB-model-derivations/SSBMF-YFB-model-derivation-full.pdf`. The script
`verify_derivation.R` in the same folder checks every update against a brute-force evaluation of
the objective and against the code.

# Appendix B. Changes since the October 16 version {#sec-appendix-b .unnumbered}

- **Preprocessing.** Every RNA-seq cohort is logged once. The D4 gene set has
  `r big(genes$n_genes[genes$arm == "single"])` genes instead of
  `r big(genes$n_genes[genes$arm == "double"])`, `r big(genes$overlap_with_frozen[genes$arm == "single"])`
  of them shared.
- **Model.** The proposed model is the survival-weighted fit of @sec-model. The $\alpha_F = 0$
  configuration is a historical reference.
- **Objective.** The Gaussian log-normalizer in the KL term of the activity update is now counted
  once per observation. This changes when the stopping rule fires.
- **Orientation.** Two comparator scripts that chose each cohort's risk direction from its own
  outcomes now use the training direction. No reported concordance changed.
- **Sign correction.** The post-fit sign flip was removed from both fitters.
- **Simulation calibration.** Calibration slopes in simulation use exact event times.
- **Multimodal model.** Moved to proposed work.
